title: Axeyum Theorem Correspondence
description: One adjudicated claim that two settled facts in the ledger are the same mathematical content. This is NOT a proof dependency: `depends_on` says one proof used the other, and a correspondence says the two are the same idea whether or not either proof ever mentions the other. The two are mutually exclusive by construction and `scripts/validate-correspondences.py` refuses a correspondence whose endpoints the fact ledger already connects. Everything that makes the claim strong or weak -- the transport that identifies the two, the intermediate steps and whether each one exists here, and the separation of what WE established from what mathematics knows -- is structured data, never tone.

id.description: `X:` for cross-reference. Distinct from `F:` facts, `C:` concepts, `K:` overlay entities and `L:` overlay links, so an id says what kind of thing it names.

correspondence_kind.description: `carrier-transport`: the same law stated over two different carriers -- checkable, because stripping the carrier from both formal statements must leave the same string. `independent-formalization`: the same classical theorem formalized twice by DIFFERENT proof routes; the endpoints' formal statements are in different languages so no structural check is available and the validator says so. `specialization`: endpoints[0] is what endpoints[1] becomes under the substitution named in `transport`; ordered, never symmetric.

endpoints.description: Exactly two fact ids. Facts, not kernel declarations: a fact is the only object in this repository that carries a formal statement, and the kernel projection's rows carry an id, a kind and an axiom footprint but no type. A correspondence anchored on a projection row could not be checked against anything, which is the failure mode this file exists to avoid. For `specialization` the order is load-bearing: endpoints[0] specializes endpoints[1].

claim.description: What is the same about the two, in prose. The floor is set from measured practice next door: math-education's `bridges_to` reasons run 75-328 characters with a median of 190, and its SHACL floor of 10 never fired.

transport.description: The SPECIFIC map, cast, substitution or instantiation that identifies the two statements. `they are related` is not a transport; `n as an integer via Int.ofNat, with Int.fib agreeing with Nat.fib there` is.

derivation_status.description: What WE established about the correspondence itself, on the same axis as a fact's `epistemic_status`. `asserted`: nobody has written down a route, and `via` is empty. `route-recorded`: `via` names the intermediate steps and every one of them resolves to something that exists here, but nothing composes them. `mechanized-here`: a checked artifact establishes the equivalence, and `evidence` carries the command that re-derives it.

external_status.description: What MATHEMATICS knows about the correspondence, on the same axis as a fact's `external_status`. `novel-here` claims the connection itself is new, and the validator requires `derivation_status: mechanized-here` to back it.

step.description: One intermediate result the route needs.

ref.description: The object that supplies this step: an `F:` fact id, or `kernel:<Declaration.Name>` resolved against artifacts/autogenesis/kernel-dependency-projection-v1.json. `null` means the step is MISSING here -- a named gap, and the reason a route with any null cannot be `mechanized-here`.

via.description: The ordered route from one endpoint to the other. Empty exactly when `derivation_status` is `asserted`. Every non-null `ref` must resolve; a step naming an object that does not exist is the failure this array exists to make impossible.

checker_command.description: A command whose EXIT STATUS depends on what it found. Required non-empty, and required at all, only for `mechanized-here`.
